mainTopic: The end of שבנא's story, readings of ״כי השתות יהרסון״ and ״תושיה״, and which witnesses are disqualified and when
overview: The amud opens by finishing the story of שבנא, who tried to surrender ירושלים to סנחריב. His followers abandon him, and the soldiers of אשור drag him behind their horses. רבי אלעזר proves from the word סוכן that שבנא was a בעל הנאה. Three אמוראים then explain the פסוק ״כי השתות יהרסון צדיק מה פעל״, and the גמרא checks each reading against the word ״השתות״. That leads to teachings about ״תושיה״ as a name for the תורה, and to a discussion of whether worry can disturb Torah learning. The גמרא then returns to the משנה about invalid witnesses. It rules like רבי יהודה, requires a הכרזה in בית דין, and teaches that a robber by Torah law needs no announcement. רב נחמן's rulings follow, about people who take support in a shameful way, people suspected of עריות, and harvest-season thieves. The amud ends with gravediggers who buried on יום טוב and are still valid witnesses because they thought they were doing a מצוה, and then opens a new statement with ״איתמר״ that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The soldiers of אשור ask שבנא where his followers are
steps.stepSummary: The soldiers of אשור ask שבנא where his camp is. He admits his people backed out, and they accuse him of making fun of them.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: Where is your camp? He said: They backed out on me. They said to him: If so, you were just mocking us!
steps.whatsHappening: The story of שבנא continues. When he arrives alone, the soldiers of אשור ask where his followers are, and he admits they abandoned him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שבנא had made סנחריב believe a large group would surrender with him. Now that he shows up alone, the soldiers feel tricked and accuse him of mocking them. This sets up the punishment in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Your camp, your group of followers
They backed out on me, they changed their minds
You are mocking us, making fools of us

phrases.english: They said to him: Where is your camp?
phrases.notes: "They" are the soldiers of אשור, the army of סנחריב.

phrases.english: He said: They backed out on me.
They said to him: If so,
you are mocking us!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַרוּ לֵיהּ: מַשְׁירְיָיתָךְ הֵיכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story of שבנא from earlier on the דף.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שבנא's followers abandoned him, and the soldiers of אשור felt he had tricked them.

steps.title: שבנא is dragged behind horses
steps.stepSummary: The soldiers pierce שבנא's heels, tie him to their horses' tails, and drag him over thorns.
steps.simpleTranslation: They pierced holes in his heels, tied him to the tails of their horses, and dragged him over thorns and briers.
steps.whatsHappening: The story ends with the harsh punishment the soldiers of אשור gave שבנא for misleading them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The man who betrayed his own people ends up humiliated and tortured by the very side he tried to join. This closes the story of שבנא.
steps.whatToRemember: שבנא tried to betray חזקיה and ירושלים, but his followers abandoned him and אשור punished him cruelly.

phrases.english: They pierced him in his heels
and tied him to the tails of their horses,
and they dragged him
over the thorns and over the briers.

steps.triggerLanguage: נְקָבוּהוּ בַּעֲקָבָיו וּתְלָאוּהוּ בְּזַנְבֵי סוּסֵיהֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The result of the soldiers feeling mocked in step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שבנא was punished by being dragged behind horses over thorns.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר says שבנא chased pleasure
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר states that שבנא was a בעל הנאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר says: שבנא was a person who chased pleasure.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר adds a new detail about שבנא's character: he was a pleasure-seeker. His proof comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a new claim about שבנא, separate from the surrender story. רבי אלעזר is about to support it from a word in the פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: שבנא, an official in חזקיה's court who tried to surrender to סנחריב
A person who chases pleasure, a hedonist

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar says:
Shebna was a pleasure-seeker.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: שֶׁבְנָא בַּעַל הֲנָאָה הָיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the story to a new statement about שבנא's character.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שבנא was a בעל הנאה.

steps.title: Proof from the word סוכן
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר links ״הסוכן״ said about שבנא to ״סוכנת״ said about אבישג, who kept דוד המלך warm.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is written here: “Go, get yourself to this steward [הסוכן],” and it is written there: “And let her be a companion [סוכנת] to him.”
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר proves his claim by comparing the same word used in two different פסוקים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ישעיה calls שבנא ״הסוכן״. In מלכים, the same root describes אבישג, who was brought to lie with דוד and keep him warm. Because the word is shared, רבי אלעזר reads physical pleasure into שבנא's title.

keyTerms.meaning: It is written here... and it is written there, the standard wording for comparing two פסוקים
Steward or official, the title given to שבנא
Companion or attendant, said about אבישג

phrases.english: It is written here:
“Go, get yourself to this steward,”
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 22:15, where the פסוק goes on to name שבנא.

phrases.english: and it is written there:
“And let her be a companion to him.”
phrases.notes: מלכים א 1:2, about אבישג, who was brought to keep the elderly דוד warm.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּתִיב הָכָא: ״לֶךְ בֹּא אֶל הַסֹּכֵן הַזֶּה״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source for רבי אלעזר's claim in step 3.
steps.raayaObject: That שבנא was a בעל הנאה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The shared word סוכן / סוכנת in ישעיהו 22:15 and מלכים א 1:2.

steps.title: Another verse: when the foundations are destroyed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings the next פסוק in תהלים, ״כי השתות יהרסון צדיק מה פעל״.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it says: “When the foundations are destroyed, what has the Righteous One done?”
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes another פסוק connected to this story. This sets up the explanations of the פסוק that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier the גמרא used ״כי הנה הרשעים ידרכון קשת״ for שבנא's plot. ״ואומר״ brings the very next פסוק in תהלים, and its meaning will now be debated.

keyTerms.meaning: And it says, introducing another פסוק
The foundations; some read it as plans or intentions
What has the Righteous One done? Here the Righteous One is הקב״ה

steps.confusionAlert: ״צדיק״ here means הקב״ה, not a righteous person. The question is what הקב״ה would have accomplished.

phrases.english: And it says:
phrases.notes: This is the פסוק right after ״כי הנה הרשעים ידרכון קשת״, which was quoted earlier.

phrases.english: “When the foundations are destroyed,
phrases.notes: תהלים 11:3

phrases.english: what has the Righteous One done?”

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאוֹמֵר: ״כִּי הַשָּׁתוֹת יֵהָרֵסוּן צַדִּיק מַה פָּעָל״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the פסוקים in תהלים that were applied to this story earlier on the דף.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The פסוק ״כי השתות יהרסון צדיק מה פעל״ relates to the events of שבנא and סנחריב.

steps.title: רב יהודה and רב עינא explain the verse
steps.stepSummary: One reads the פסוק as being about חזקיה and his camp, and the other as being about the בית המקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה and רב עינא: One says: If חזקיה and his group were destroyed, what would the Righteous One have done? And one says: If the בית המקדש were destroyed, what would the Righteous One have done?
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים give two different explanations of what ״השתות״, the things that might be destroyed, refers to.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One says the ״foundations″ are חזקיה and his loyal followers. The other says they are the בית המקדש. Either way, the פסוק asks what הקב״ה would have gained if that had been destroyed.

keyTerms.meaning: One says... and one says; we are not told which רב said which
חזקיה and his group of supporters

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda and Rav Eina:
One says:
If Hezekiah and his group were destroyed,
what would the Righteous One have done?
And one says:
If the Temple were destroyed,
what would the Righteous One have done?

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב יְהוּדָה וְרַב עֵינָא, חַד אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the פסוק quoted in step 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ״השתות″ are either חזקיה and his camp, or the בית המקדש.

steps.title: עולא: the wicked one's plans
steps.stepSummary: עולא reads the פסוק as being about סנחריב's plans: if they had not been destroyed, what would הקב״ה have done?
steps.simpleTranslation: And עולא says: If the plans of that wicked man were not destroyed, what would the Righteous One have done?
steps.whatsHappening: עולא offers a third explanation. In his reading, the things being destroyed are the evil plans of סנחריב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first two readings speak of something good, חזקיה or the בית המקדש, being destroyed. עולא flips this: the ״השתות″ are the enemy's plans, and they must be destroyed, or else what has הקב״ה accomplished?

phrases.english: And Ulla says:
If the plans of that wicked man
were not destroyed,
what would the Righteous One have done?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְעוּלָּא אָמַר: אִילּוּ מַחְשְׁבוֹתָיו שֶׁל אוֹתוֹ רָשָׁע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a third reading that differs from both readings in step 6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ״השתות″ are סנחריב's plans, which were destroyed.

steps.title: עולא's reading fits the word ״השתות״
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא grants that עולא's reading explains the word ״השתות״ well. This prepares a challenge against the other two readings.
steps.simpleTranslation: It works well according to the one who says “if the plans of that wicked man,” because that is why it is written: “When the foundations [השתות] are destroyed.”
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts weighing the three readings against the actual wording. It first grants that עולא's reading fits ״השתות״. Step 9 shows that the בית המקדש reading fits too, and step 10 brings the real challenge, against the חזקיה reading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ״בשלמא״ means: this opinion is fine. According to עולא, ״השתות״ are plans, and the פסוק says they are destroyed, which is exactly what happened to סנחריב. Coming next is the question of how the other readings explain this word.

keyTerms.meaning: It works well for... This sets up a challenge against a different opinion
According to the one who says
That is why it is written

steps.confusionAlert: ״בשלמא″ is only the first half of a challenge. The real question, ״אלא למאן דאמר חזקיה וסיעתו...״, comes in step 10.

phrases.english: It works well according to the one who says:
“If the plans of that wicked man,”
that is why it is written:
“When the foundations are destroyed.”
phrases.notes: In this reading, ״השתות״ means plans, so the פסוק describes סנחריב's plans being destroyed.

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the three readings from steps 6 and 7 against the wording of the פסוק.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that ״השתות״ refers to חזקיה and his camp.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: עולא's reading clearly fits ״השתות״ (plans), and the בית המקדש reading fits through the אבן שתיה (step 9). That leaves the חזקיה reading needing a source where צדיקים are called ״שתות״.

steps.title: The בית המקדש reading also explains the word
steps.stepSummary: The reading that the פסוק is about the בית המקדש also fits the word ״השתות״, because a משנה says the stone there was called ״שתיה״.
steps.simpleTranslation: The one who says the פסוק is about the בית המקדש can also explain the word well. A משנה teaches that there was a stone there from the days of the early prophets, and it was called ״שתיה״ (the Foundation Stone).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the reading about the בית המקדש also explains ״השתות״ well. This sets up the challenge against the remaining reading, about חזקיה and his camp.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ״השתות״ sounds like ״שתיה״, the name of the foundation stone in the בית המקדש. So destroying ״the foundations″ fits the destruction of the בית המקדש. Only the חזקיה reading is left without a clear source.

keyTerms.meaning: The Foundation Stone in the קודש הקדשים

phrases.english: And according to the one who says it is about the Temple, it also fits –
as we learned: there was a stone there
phrases.notes: This is a משנה in יומא. "There" means in the קודש הקדשים.

phrases.english: from the days of the early prophets,
and it was called "Foundation" (שתיה).

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְמַאן דְּאָמַר בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ, נָמֵי – דִּתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues step 8: after עולא's reading, the בית המקדש reading is also shown to fit the word.
steps.raayaObject: That ״השתות״ fits the reading about the בית המקדש
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about the אבן שתיה in the קודש הקדשים

steps.title: Where are righteous people called 'foundations'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the reading that the פסוק is about חזקיה and his camp: where are צדיקים ever called ״שתות״?
steps.simpleTranslation: But the one who says the פסוק is about חזקיה and his camp: where do we find that righteous people are called ״שתות״?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now asks the challenge that step 8 was building toward. The חזקיה reading needs a source showing that צדיקים are called ״foundations″.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The other two readings each have a clear link to the word ״השתות״. The חזקיה reading has no clear link yet, so the גמרא asks for one.

phrases.english: But according to the one who says it is about חזקיה and his camp,
where do we find righteous people
who are called "foundations"?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר חִזְקִיָּה וְסִיעָתוֹ, הֵיכָא אַשְׁכְּחַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After both other readings were shown to fit, this challenges the remaining one.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that ״השתות״ refers to חזקיה and his camp
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: There is no known source calling צדיקים ״שתות״, so the reading seems not to fit the word.

steps.title: The world is set upon the righteous
steps.stepSummary: The answer comes from a פסוק saying that ה׳ set the world upon the ״pillars of the earth″. That shows צדיקים are the foundations of the world.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: "For the pillars of the earth are ה׳'s, and He set (וישת) the world upon them."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge with a פסוק showing that the world rests on צדיקים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word ״וישת″ (He set) sounds like ״שתות״. Since the world is set on the righteous, they can be called ״foundations″. So the חזקיה reading fits too.

phrases.english: As it is written: "For the pillars of the earth are the LORD's,
phrases.notes: שמואל א 2:8

phrases.english: and He set the world upon them."

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּכְתִיב: ״כִּי לַה׳ מְצֻקֵי אֶרֶץ וַיָּשֶׁת עֲלֵיהֶם תֵּבֵל״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Brings a פסוק showing the needed usage
steps.terutzHavaAmina: צדיקים are never called ״שתות״, so the חזקיה reading does not fit the word.
steps.terutzMaskana: The world is set (וישת) upon the righteous, so they are its foundations.

steps.title: A second source: 'great wisdom' (תושיה)
steps.stepSummary: A second answer: the source can be ״הפליא עצה הגדיל תושיה״. The word ״תושיה״ is read as connected to ״שתות״.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want, say the source is from here: "Wonderful is His counsel, great is His wisdom (תושיה)."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers another פסוק as the source for calling righteous, wise people ״שתות״.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word ״תושיה״ is heard as related to ״שתות״. That makes the wise and righteous the ״foundations″. The third explanation of ״תושיה״ below (step 15) spells out this link: the world is ״משותת″ (founded) on the תורה.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you want, say (introduces another answer)
Wisdom; a name for the תורה

phrases.english: And if you wish, say it is from here:
"Wonderful is His counsel, great is His wisdom."
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 28:29

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא מֵהָכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second, alternative answer to the challenge of step 10.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Without a source, the חזקיה reading would lack support.
steps.terutzMaskana: ״תושיה״ shows that wise, righteous people can be called ״שתות″.
steps.whyThisMatters: The word ״תושיה״ in this פסוק opens the next section, where רבי חנן explains the name.

steps.title: Torah weakens a person's strength
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנן says the תורה is called ״תושיה״ because it ״weakens″ (מתשת) a person's strength.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנן said: Why is it called ״תושיה″? Because it weakens a person's strength.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings רבי חנן's first explanation of why the תורה is called ״תושיה״.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word ״תושיה״ is read as sounding like ״מתשת″, meaning weakens. Learning תורה takes so much effort that it tires a person out.

phrases.english: Rabbi Ḥanan said:
Why is its name called "tushiyya"?
phrases.notes: "Its" means the תורה, the wisdom the פסוק just praised.

phrases.aramaic: מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהִיא מַתֶּשֶׁת כֹּחוֹ שֶׁל אָדָם.
phrases.english: Because it weakens the strength of a person.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי חָנָן: לָמָּה נִקְרָא שְׁמָהּ תּוּשִׁיָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Picks up the word ״תושיה״ from the פסוק in step 12 and explains it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The תורה is called ״תושיה״ because it wears down a person's strength.

steps.title: Torah was given quietly because of the שטן
steps.stepSummary: Another explanation: ״תושיה״ hints that the תורה was given quietly, because of the שטן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another explanation: ״תושיה״ means that it was given quietly, because of the שטן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second explanation of the name ״תושיה״.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the word is heard as hinting to ״שניתנה בחשאי″, meaning given in secret. It was given quietly because of the שטן.

phrases.english: Another explanation: tushiyya –
that it was given quietly because of the Satan.
phrases.notes: The letters of ״תושיה״ are being heard as a hint to ״שניתנה בחשאי״, given quietly.

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּבָר אַחֵר: תּוּשִׁיָּה – שֶׁנִּיתְּנָה בַּחֲשַׁאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, alternative explanation of the same word.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The תורה is called ״תושיה״ because it was given quietly, because of the שטן.

steps.title: The world is founded on Torah
steps.stepSummary: A third explanation: ״תושיה״ means matters that seem like ״תוהו″ (empty), yet the world is founded (משותת) on them.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another explanation: ״תושיה״ means things that seem like emptiness, yet the world is founded on them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a third explanation of ״תושיה״, and this one ties back to the idea of ״foundations″.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ״תושיה״ is split into ״תוהו″ (emptiness) and ״משותת″ (founded). Things in the תורה may look strange or empty, but the whole world stands on them. This shows the link between ״תושיה״ and ״שתות״ used in step 12.

keyTerms.meaning: Emptiness; something that looks without substance

steps.whatToRemember: The חזקיה reading is supported because the world rests on the righteous and on their תורה. They are the true ״שתות״ (foundations). The three explanations of ״תושיה״ are: it wears a person down (said by רבי חנן), it was given quietly, and the world is founded on it.

phrases.english: Another explanation: tushiyya –
matters that seem empty
upon which the world is founded.

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּבָר אַחֵר: תּוּשִׁיָּה – דְּבָרִים שֶׁל תּוֹהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third explanation of ״תושיה״. It connects back to the ״foundations″ theme of steps 10-12.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The תורה is called ״תושיה״ because the world is founded on its seemingly strange matters.

steps.title: Worry can disturb even Torah learning
steps.stepSummary: עולא teaches that worrying thoughts can disturb a person even when he learns Torah, based on a פסוק in איוב that uses the word תושיה.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא says: worry can affect a person even in Torah learning. The פסוק says, "He frustrates the thoughts of the crafty, so that their hands cannot accomplish תושיה," and תושיה means Torah.
steps.whatsHappening: עולא adds one more teaching built on the word תושיה. He says worry and anxiety can get in the way of Torah learning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The previous steps showed that תושיה can mean Torah. עולא uses that idea to read the פסוק as saying that troubled thoughts can stop a person's hands from doing תושיה, which means Torah. So even a holy activity like learning can be disturbed by worry.

keyTerms.meaning: Thought; here, worrying or anxious thoughts

phrases.english: Ulla says:
Worry has an effect even on words of Torah,
as it is said:
"He frustrates the thoughts of the crafty,
phrases.notes: איוב 5:12

phrases.english: so that their hands cannot accomplish תושיה."
phrases.notes: Remember from the last few steps that תושיה is a name for the Torah.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר עוּלָּא: מַחְשָׁבָה מוֹעֶלֶת אֲפִילּוּ לְדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the series of teachings about the word תושיה as a name for Torah.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Worrying thoughts can disturb even Torah learning.

steps.title: Learning for its own sake is protected from worry
steps.stepSummary: רבה limits עולא's teaching. If a person learns Torah לשמה, worry cannot disturb him, based on a פסוק in משלי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה says: if people are learning Torah for its own sake, worry has no effect on them. The פסוק says, "There are many thoughts in a person's heart, but the counsel of ה׳, that will stand." Counsel that contains the word of ה׳ will stand forever.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה adds a limit to עולא's teaching. Worry cannot disturb someone who learns Torah לשמה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עולא said worry can affect Torah learning. רבה says this is not true when the learning is לשמה. He reads "עצת ה׳" as counsel that carries the word of ה׳, which is Torah, so it stands firm and many anxious thoughts cannot knock it down.

keyTerms.meaning: For its own sake; learning Torah purely to know it and serve ה׳

phrases.english: Rabba says:
If they are engaged in it for its own sake,
it has no effect,
as it is said:
"There are many thoughts in a person's heart,
phrases.notes: משלי 19:21

phrases.english: but the counsel of ה׳, that will stand."
Counsel that has the word of ה׳ in it
is what will stand forever.

steps.whatToRemember: עולא says worry can disturb Torah learning. רבה says it cannot disturb learning that is לשמה.
steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה: אִם עֲסוּקִין לִשְׁמָהּ, אֵינָהּ מוֹעֶלֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits עולא's statement by giving an exception for learning לשמה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Worry cannot disturb Torah that is learned for its own sake.

steps.title: The הלכה follows רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to the משנה, which quoted רבי יהודה asking "When?". רבי אבהו, in the name of רבי אלעזר, rules like רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: רבי יהודה said, "When?" רבי אבהו said in the name of רבי אלעזר: the הלכה follows רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The talk about תושיה is over, and the גמרא returns to the משנה. It quotes רבי יהודה's words from the משנה and rules that the halacha follows him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, רבי יהודה limited the rule that gamblers, people who lend with interest, and similar people cannot be witnesses. He said this applies only when they have no other job. רבי אלעזר rules like him, so people who also have a proper occupation are not disqualified.

keyTerms.meaning: When? It opens a limit on a rule

steps.confusionAlert: "אמר רבי יהודה אימתי" is not a new statement. It is just the גמרא pointing back to words already in the משנה, so it can give a ruling on them.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: When?

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר:
phrases.english: Rabbi Abbahu says that Rabbi Elazar says:
The halacha follows Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.whyThisMatters: This gives the practical ruling: someone is disqualified as a witness for these activities only if he has no other occupation.
steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אֵימָתַי. אָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the side discussion about תושיה and goes back to the משנה's rules about disqualified witnesses.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The halacha follows רבי יהודה, who limits the disqualification to people with no other occupation.

steps.title: Disqualification needs a public announcement in court
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו, in the name of רבי אלעזר, also rules that all of these people need an announcement in בית דין before they are disqualified.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אבהו said in the name of רבי אלעזר: all of them need a public announcement in בית דין.
steps.whatsHappening: A second ruling from the same teachers. Each disqualified type of person loses his right to be a witness only after בית דין announces it publicly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This adds a step of procedure. Doing the bad behavior does not cancel a person's testimony by itself. Only once בית דין publicly announces that he was found doing it is he treated as disqualified.

keyTerms.meaning: All of them, meaning all the disqualified people listed in the משנה

steps.whatToRemember: Two rulings from רבי אבהו in the name of רבי אלעזר: the halacha follows רבי יהודה, and every disqualification needs an announcement in בית דין.

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר:
phrases.english: And Rabbi Abbahu says that Rabbi Elazar says:
All of them require a proclamation in the court.

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the practical moment when a person stops being a valid witness. It is the court's announcement, not just his behavior.
steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: כּוּלָּן צְרִיכִין הַכְרָזָה בְּבֵית דִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second ruling from the same chain of teachers, about the same group of disqualified witnesses.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: All the disqualified witnesses in the משנה are disqualified only after a public announcement in בית דין.

steps.title: Does a shepherd need an announcement?
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא and רבינא argue whether a shepherd needs a הכרזה in בית דין before he is disqualified as a witness.
steps.simpleTranslation: About a shepherd, רב אחא and רבינא disagree. One says he needs an announcement, and one says he does not need an announcement.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא applies the rule from step 19, that disqualified people need an announcement, to the case of a shepherd. Two אמוראים argue about it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 19 said all the disqualified people need a הכרזה in בית דין before they lose their status as witnesses. Here the question is whether a shepherd is also included in that rule, or whether he is disqualified automatically. One view: he needs a הכרזה like everyone else. The other view: he is disqualified even without one.

keyTerms.meaning: A public announcement in בית דין that someone is disqualified
One said (we are not told which אמורא held which view)

phrases.english: A shepherd: they disagree about it
רב אחא and רבינא:
One says he needs an announcement,
and one says he does not need an announcement.

steps.triggerLanguage: פְּלִיגִי בַּהּ רַב אַחָא וְרָבִינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies step 19's rule that disqualified people need an announcement to the specific case of a shepherd, where there is a disagreement.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There is a disagreement: one view says a shepherd needs a הכרזה before he is disqualified, the other says he is disqualified without one.

steps.title: רב's statement seems to fit only one view
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says רב's statement that an ordinary shepherd is disqualified fits the view that no announcement is needed. It asks how the other view explains it.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense for the one who says no announcement is needed. That is what רב יהודה said in the name of רב: an ordinary shepherd is disqualified. But for the one who says an announcement is needed, what does 'an ordinary shepherd is disqualified' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the view that a shepherd needs an announcement. It quotes רב, who said an ordinary shepherd is disqualified, which sounds automatic.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'an ordinary shepherd is disqualified' sound like any shepherd is disqualified on the spot, with no announcement. That fits the view that no הכרזה is needed. So the view that requires a הכרזה seems to go against רב, and the גמרא asks how it understands רב's words.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense (for one side); sets up a challenge to the other side
An ordinary shepherd, with no special details known about him
But (introduces the side that has a difficulty)

phrases.english: It makes sense according to the one who says
he does not need an announcement,

phrases.aramaic: הַיְינוּ דְּאָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: that is what רב יהודה said in the name of רב:
an ordinary shepherd is disqualified.
But according to the one who says he needs an announcement,
what does 'an ordinary shepherd is disqualified' mean?

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר לָא בָּעֵי הַכְרָזָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests both sides of the disagreement in step 20 against רב's statement and finds a difficulty for the view that requires a הכרזה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that a shepherd needs a הכרזה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב said an ordinary shepherd is disqualified, which sounds automatic. That seems to leave no room for an announcement.

steps.title: Even an ordinary shepherd gets announced
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רב means we make the announcement about an ordinary shepherd too, without needing more proof.
steps.simpleTranslation: It means that even in an ordinary case, we announce about him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge, so the view that requires a הכרזה can keep רב's statement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב was not saying the shepherd is disqualified without a הכרזה. He was saying that being an ordinary shepherd is already enough reason for בית דין to announce him as disqualified. We do not need extra evidence that he grazed his animals in other people's fields. So רב's statement fits both views.

keyTerms.meaning: In an ordinary case, with nothing extra known

steps.confusionAlert: This answer does not say a shepherd needs no announcement. It says the announcement is still made, and that being an ordinary shepherd is enough reason to make it.

phrases.english: That in an ordinary case we announce about him.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּבִסְתָמָא מַכְרְזִינַן עֲלֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 21 by reading רב's words differently.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב's 'an ordinary shepherd is disqualified' means he is disqualified automatically, with no announcement.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב means an ordinary shepherd is enough reason for בית דין to announce him, so the announcement is still required.
steps.whatToRemember: Both views can live with רב's statement. The view that requires a הכרזה reads it as: any ordinary shepherd gets announced, even without extra proof.

steps.title: A gift document signed by two robbers
steps.stepSummary: A story: a gift document had two robbers signed as witnesses. רב פפא בר שמואל wanted to accept it because no announcement had been made about them.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a gift document signed by two robbers. רב פפא בר שמואל thought he should accept it as valid, since no announcement had been made about them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a real-life case that tests the rule of הכרזה. This step is a setup for the reaction that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פפא בר שמואל used the rule from step 19: a disqualified person is only disqualified after a הכרזה. These robbers had never been announced, so he thought their signatures were still good. The word סבר ('he thought') hints that someone is about to challenge his plan.

keyTerms.meaning: A gift; here, a gift document

phrases.english: There was a certain gift document
on which two robbers were signed,

phrases.aramaic: סְבַר רַב פָּפָּא בַּר שְׁמוּאֵל לְאַכְשׁוֹרַהּ,
phrases.english: רב פפא בר שמואל thought to declare it valid,
since no announcement had been made about them.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהִיא מַתָּנָה דַּהֲווֹ חֲתִימִי עֲלַהּ תְּרֵין גַּזְלָנִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the shepherd discussion to a real case that applies step 19's rule of הכרזה to robbers.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב פפא בר שמואל's first thought: witnesses who are robbers but were never announced are still valid, so the document is good.

steps.title: רבא: A Torah-law robber needs no announcement
steps.stepSummary: רבא rejects רב פפא בר שמואל's plan to accept the document. The announcement rule covers only robbers by rabbinic law. Robbers by Torah law are disqualified automatically.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: Fine, we need an announcement for a robber whose robbery is only forbidden by the רבנן. But for a robber whose robbery is forbidden by the Torah, do we need an announcement? (Of course not!)
steps.whatsHappening: רבא pushes back on רב פפא בר שמואל, who wanted to accept a document signed by two robbers because no announcement had been made about them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא splits robbers into two groups. A גזלן דרבנן (like a gambler) is disqualified only after a public announcement in בית דין. A גזלן דאורייתא is already plainly a רשע under Torah law, so he is invalid right away. That means the two robbers on the document were never valid witnesses.

keyTerms.meaning: A 'robber' whose act is forbidden only by rabbinic law
A robber whose act is forbidden by Torah law
'Granted that...' (admits one point to set up a contrast)
'Do we need?' (a question that expects the answer 'no')

steps.whatToRemember: An announcement is needed only for rabbinic-level robbers. Torah-level robbers are disqualified automatically.
steps.confusionAlert: רבא's question is not a real question. It means: 'Obviously we do not need an announcement for a Torah-law robber!'
steps.whyThisMatters: This closes the discussion of הכרזה. It tells us exactly which disqualified witnesses need a public announcement and which do not.

phrases.english: Rava said to him:
Granted that we require an announcement
for a robber by rabbinic law,
for a robber by Torah law
do we require an announcement?
phrases.notes: He means: certainly not. Such a robber is invalid right away.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא: נְהִי דְּבָעֵינַן הַכְרָזָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רב פפא בר שמואל's reasoning in the story from step 23.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The idea that a robber by Torah law needs an announcement before he is disqualified.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רב פפא בר שמואל applied the announcement rule, which was made for rabbinic-level robbers, to robbers by Torah law.

steps.title: A memory aid for the next three teachings
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives a סימן (memory aid) listing the topics of the next three teachings about invalid witnesses: 'something', 'forbidden relations', and 'thief'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Memory aid: 'Something', 'forbidden relations', 'thief'.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא is preparing the next three teachings by giving one keyword for each, so we can remember their order.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each keyword points to an upcoming statement. 'דבר' points to אוכלי דבר אחר, 'עריות' to a teaching about forbidden relations, and 'גנב' to a teaching about a thief. The memory aid adds no new law of its own.

keyTerms.meaning: A memory aid that lists keywords for the teachings that follow

phrases.english: A mnemonic:
Something, and forbidden relations, thief.
phrases.notes: Each word is a hint for one of the next three teachings. 'Something' is the one right after this.

steps.triggerLanguage: סִימָן: דָּבָר, וַעֲרָיוֹת, גַּנָּב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new set of teachings about who is disqualified as a witness.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No ruling. It only lists the order of the coming teachings.

steps.title: רב נחמן: Those who 'eat something else' are invalid witnesses
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן rules that people who 'eat something else' (דבר אחר) are disqualified from testifying.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן says: Those who eat 'something else' are disqualified from being witnesses.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן adds a new type of person who cannot serve as a witness. This is the first teaching from the memory aid ('something').
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'דבר אחר' is a polite way of avoiding a word. It usually refers to pig. From the limits the גמרא sets in the next step (public versus private, 'his livelihood'), it seems to be about a person who takes support from non-Jews in a way that shames himself and the Jewish people. Someone willing to do this for money is treated like a person who is not trustworthy as a witness.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Something else'; a polite phrase used instead of saying 'pig'

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read this as being only about eating non-kosher food. The limits in the next step show the ruling is about a shameful way of getting support, not about a food prohibition by itself.

phrases.english: Rav Naḥman says:
Those who eat something else
phrases.notes: 'Something else' is a polite way of not saying 'pig'. The next lines show it is about taking support in a shameful way.

phrases.english: are disqualified from testimony.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן: אוֹכְלֵי דָּבָר אַחֵר פְּסוּלִין לְעֵדוּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This is the first teaching listed in the memory aid ('דבר').
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Those who 'eat something else' are invalid as witnesses.

steps.title: Limits: only in public, and only if he could have managed privately
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא narrows רב נחמן's rule. It applies only when the act is done in public. Even in public, it applies only if the person could have supported himself privately. If this is his only way to live, he is not disqualified.
steps.simpleTranslation: This applies in public, but not in private. And even in public, we said it only when he could support himself privately and still shames himself in public. But if he has no other way, it is his livelihood (and he is not disqualified).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא puts two limits on רב נחמן's ruling, so that it covers only someone who shames himself for no need.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Limit 1: a person who does it in private is not disqualified. Limit 2: even a person who does it in public is disqualified only if he had a private option and chose public shame anyway. A person who has no other way to survive is not considered wicked, because this is simply how he stays alive.

keyTerms.meaning: To support himself (to get his food)
His livelihood, how he stays alive

steps.whatToRemember: A person is disqualified only for needless public self-shaming. Doing it privately, or doing it publicly because there is no other way to survive, does not disqualify him.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the disqualification is about the person's choice to bring shame for no need, not about the act in every situation.

phrases.english: This applies in public,
but in private, not.
And even in public we said it only
where it is possible for him
to support himself in private,
and he shames himself in public.
But if it is not possible for him,
it is his livelihood.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנֵי מִילֵּי בְּפַרְהֶסְיָא, אֲבָל בְּצִינְעָה לָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows רב נחמן's rule from step 26.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The disqualification applies only to public acts done when a private option was available. It does not apply when this is the person's only means of support.

steps.title: A man suspected of forbidden relations can testify
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן rules that someone suspected of עריות is still a valid witness.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: Someone suspected of forbidden relations is fit to testify.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the second topic from the memory aid, 'forbidden relations.' רב נחמן says that being suspected of עריות does not disqualify a person as a witness.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 26, people who 'eat דבר אחר' in public were disqualified. Here רב נחמן gives the opposite result for a different sin: a suspicion of עריות does not cost a person his status as a witness.

keyTerms.meaning: Suspected; there is a rumor that he did something wrong
Forbidden relations, such as with a married woman

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said:
One who is suspected of forbidden relations
is fit to testify.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן: הֶחָשׁוּד עַל הָעֲרָיוֹת כָּשֵׁר לְעֵדוּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the second topic listed in the memory aid of step 25.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person suspected of עריות remains a valid witness.

steps.title: רב ששת objects: he deserves lashes, yet he is valid?
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת is shocked. This sin carries forty lashes, so how can the person still be a valid witness?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said: Answer me, my master! He deserves forty lashes on his shoulders, and you call him fit?
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת challenges רב נחמן's ruling. He asks how someone who gets forty lashes over this could be a kosher witness.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The attack is simple. This is a serious Torah sin, serious enough for lashes. רב ששת assumes that someone like this should be disqualified the same way other sinners are. The גמרא does not record a reply here.

keyTerms.meaning: Answer me, my master; a respectful but sharp way to open a challenge
Forty, referring to the forty lashes

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet said:
Answer me, my master:
forty [lashes] are on his shoulders
and he is fit?

steps.triggerLanguage: עֲנִי מָרִי, אַרְבְּעִין בְּכַתְפֵּיהּ וְכָשֵׁר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly challenges רב נחמן's ruling.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's ruling that someone suspected of עריות is a valid witness.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A sin that carries forty lashes should disqualify the sinner from testifying.

steps.title: רבא: he cannot testify about a married woman
steps.stepSummary: רבא says that even רב נחמן agrees this man is disqualified from testimony about a woman's marital status.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: And רב נחמן agrees that he is disqualified when it comes to testimony about a woman.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא sets a limit on רב נחמן's ruling. When the testimony is about a woman's marriage, this man cannot be trusted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His suspected weakness is in exactly this area, so he may have a personal motive to lie. The general ruling that he is a valid witness stays in place. Only testimony that touches his suspected sin is excluded.

keyTerms.meaning: Agrees, even according to his own view
Testimony about a woman's marital status

phrases.english: Rava said:
And Rav Nachman agrees
regarding testimony about a woman
that he is disqualified.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמוֹדֶה רַב נַחְמָן לְעִנְיַן עֵדוּת אִשָּׁה שֶׁהוּא פָּסוּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits רב נחמן's ruling from step 28.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A man suspected of עריות cannot testify about a woman's marital status.

steps.title: Only testimony that frees her is blocked
steps.stepSummary: רבינא (or רב פפא) narrows רבא's limit. The man is blocked only from testimony that takes a woman out of her marriage. Testimony that keeps her married is fine.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said, and some say רב פפא: We said this only about taking her out of marriage. But about bringing her into marriage, we have no problem.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא narrows רבא's rule even further. The disqualification applies only when his testimony would make the woman available.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If he testifies that her husband died, he might be lying so that he can have her. If he testifies that she is married, he gains nothing from it, so he is believed.

keyTerms.meaning: To take her out of her married status
To bring her into, or keep her in, married status
We have no problem with it

phrases.english: Ravina said,
and some say Rav Pappa:
We said this only to take her out,
phrases.notes: This means testimony that frees her from her marriage, such as saying that her husband died.

phrases.english: but to bring her in
we have no problem with it.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא אֲמַרַן אֶלָּא לְאַפּוֹקַהּ, אֲבָל לְעַיּוֹלַהּ – לֵית לַן בַּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows רבא's limitation from step 30.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: He is disqualified only from testimony that frees a woman from marriage, not from testimony that establishes that she is married.

steps.title: Isn't that obvious?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why we need to be told that he may testify that she is married. That seems obvious.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the need for the previous teaching. It sets up the answer that comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Why would anyone suspect him of lying to make a woman forbidden to himself? Since he has no apparent motive, the ruling seems unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious; why does this need to be said?

phrases.english: It's obvious!

steps.triggerLanguage: פְּשִׁיטָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions why the second half of step 31 needed to be said.
steps.kashyaTarget: The statement that he may testify that she is married.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: He has no reason to lie in order to make her forbidden, so the ruling seems unnecessary.

steps.title: Stolen waters are sweet, but an unmarried woman is more available
steps.stepSummary: We might have thought he would prefer her married, since forbidden things feel sweeter. The teaching shows that he really prefers her unmarried, because then she is easier to reach.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said that he likes it better this way, as it is written, 'Stolen waters are sweet.' So it teaches us that as long as she stays this way, she is more available to him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the 'obvious' question. There was a reason to suspect him even when he testifies that she is married.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק suggests that a sinner enjoys forbidden things more, so he might lie to make her 'forbidden fruit.' The teaching rejects this: an unmarried woman is more available to him, so he has no motive to lie.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said; introduces the mistaken assumption
Stolen waters are sweet; forbidden things feel more tempting

phrases.english: You might have said
this is better for him,
phrases.notes: He means that her being married to someone else might appeal to him more.

phrases.english: as it is written:
"Stolen waters are sweet, etc."?
phrases.notes: משלי 9:17

phrases.english: It teaches us
that as long as she stays this way
phrases.notes: This way means unmarried.

phrases.english: she is available to him.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַהוּ דְּתֵימָא הָא עֲדִיפָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'obvious' challenge of step 32.
steps.terutzResolutionType: מהו דתימא: shows there was a reasonable mistaken assumption to correct
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Because forbidden things feel sweeter, he might lie to make her married.
steps.terutzMaskana: An unmarried woman is more available to him, so he has no motive to lie that she is married.
steps.whatToRemember: A man suspected of עריות is a valid witness in general. He is disqualified only from testimony that frees a woman from her marriage.

steps.title: A harvest-season thief is not called a thief
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן rules that someone who steals only during the harvest seasons of ניסן and תשרי is not considered a thief for disqualifying testimony.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב נחמן said: A thief of ניסן and a thief of תשרי is not called a thief.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the third topic from the memory aid, 'thief.' רב נחמן says that a person who steals only in the harvest seasons does not lose his status as a witness.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The theft is limited to ניסן and תשרי, when produce is plentiful. Even so, רב נחמן says it does not earn the person the label 'thief' for the laws of testimony.

keyTerms.meaning: The spring month of the grain harvest
The autumn month of the fruit and grape harvest
Is not called; does not get this label

phrases.english: And Rav Nachman said:
A Nisan thief and a Tishrei thief
phrases.notes: This means someone who steals during the harvest seasons.

phrases.english: is not called a thief.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַב נַחְמָן: גַּנַּב נִיסָן וְגַנַּב תִּשְׁרֵי – לָא שְׁמֵיהּ גַּנָּב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the third topic listed in the memory aid of step 25.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who steals only in the harvest seasons is not labeled a thief and is not disqualified from testimony.

steps.title: When the seasonal-thief leniency applies
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן's leniency applies only to an אריס who takes a small amount of produce that is already fully processed.
steps.simpleTranslation: This rule applies only to a sharecropper, only to a small amount, and only to produce whose work is already finished.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets three limits on רב נחמן's ruling that a harvest-season thief is not disqualified.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only an אריס, who works the field, can talk himself into thinking he has some right to the produce. He must take only a little, and only from produce that is finished, so he can tell himself it is pay for extra work. With all three conditions his taking is not plain, deliberate theft, so he stays a valid witness.

keyTerms.meaning: And this applies only (a limiting phrase)
A sharecropper who works a field for a share of the crop

steps.confusionAlert: This does not make stealing permitted. The point is only that this person is not treated as a deliberate thief for the rules of עדות.

phrases.english: And this applies to a sharecropper,
and a small amount,
and an item whose work was completed.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָנֵי מִילֵּי בַּאֲרִיסָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows רב נחמן's ruling from step 34
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The leniency covers only an אריס who takes a small amount of finished produce.

steps.title: רב זביד disqualifies his farm workers
steps.stepSummary: One of רב זביד's farm workers stole a קב of barley and another stole a cluster of dates. רב זביד disqualified both.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב זביד's farm workers: one stole a קב of barley, and he disqualified him. Another stole a cluster of dates, and he disqualified him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a real case that shows the "small amount" condition in action.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These workers were the kind of person the leniency is about, but what they took was more than a small amount. So the leniency did not help them, and רב זביד ruled them invalid as witnesses.

keyTerms.meaning: A קב (a dry measure) of barley

phrases.english: The farm workers of Rav Zevid:
one stole a kav of barley,
and he disqualified him,
and one stole a cluster of dates,
and he disqualified him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּרֵיהּ דְּרַב זְבִיד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows the limits from step 35 being applied
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Taking more than a small amount disqualifies even a farm worker.
steps.whatToRemember: רב נחמן's leniency is narrow. Without all three conditions, the worker is a thief and cannot testify.

steps.title: Gravediggers who buried on the first day of שבועות
steps.stepSummary: Gravediggers buried someone on the first day of שבועות. רב פפא put them in נידוי and disqualified them, but רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע ruled them fit.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some gravediggers buried a person on the first day of שבועות. רב פפא excommunicated them and disqualified them from testimony. רב הונא son of רב יהושע declared them fit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new case about people who broke a יום טוב law, and two אמוראים disagree about whether they can testify.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פפא treats the burial as a sin that makes them invalid witnesses. רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע disagrees and accepts them. Steps 38-41 lay out their back-and-forth.

keyTerms.meaning: He put them in נידוי (excommunicated them)

phrases.english: Those gravediggers who buried a person
on the first day of the festival of Shavuot,
Rav Pappa excommunicated them
and disqualified them from testimony,

phrases.aramaic: וְאַכְשְׁרִינְהוּ רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ.
phrases.english: and Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua declared them fit.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנְהוּ קָבוֹרָאֵי דִּקְבוּר נַפְשָׁא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new case about who loses eligibility for עדות
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב פפא disqualifies the gravediggers. רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע declares them fit.

steps.title: רב פפא objects: they are wicked
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא challenges רב הונא: these men broke a Torah law, so how can they be valid witnesses?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said to him: But aren't they wicked people?
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא challenges רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע's ruling that the gravediggers may testify.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule is that a רשע may not testify. Since the gravediggers broke the laws of יום טוב, רב פפא argues they count as רשעים and must be disqualified.

keyTerms.meaning: Wicked people, who are not allowed to testify

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said to him:
But aren't they wicked people?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא רְשָׁעִים נִינְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב הונא's ruling from step 37
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע's ruling that the gravediggers are fit
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Breaking a Torah law makes a person a רשע, and a רשע cannot testify.

steps.title: They thought they were doing a מצוה
steps.stepSummary: The gravediggers thought burying the dead was a מצוה, so they are not רשעים.
steps.simpleTranslation: They thought they were doing a מצוה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע answers רב פפא's challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A רשע is someone who sins on purpose. These men acted wrongly, but they thought they were honoring the dead and doing a מצוה. Since they had a good intention, they are not considered wicked and can still testify.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that disqualification depends on a person's intent. A sin done with a good intention does not make someone a רשע for עדות.

phrases.english: They thought: we are doing a מצוה.
phrases.notes: The speaker is not named, but it is רב הונא answering רב פפא.

steps.triggerLanguage: סָבְרִי: מִצְוָה קָא עָבְדִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב פפא's challenge from step 38
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines the case: a sin done with a good intention
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Anyone who breaks a Torah law is a רשע and cannot testify.
steps.terutzMaskana: Someone who sinned while thinking he was doing a מצוה is not a רשע, so he stays fit to testify.
steps.whatToRemember: Only someone who sins on purpose loses his eligibility for עדות. A mistaken good intention keeps him valid.

steps.title: But we already put them in נידוי
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא pushes back: even if they first thought burial was a מצוה, they were put in נידוי for it. Shouldn't that have taught them it was wrong?
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't we put them in נידוי for this?
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא challenges רב הונא's answer from Step 39. He says the gravediggers were already put in נידוי, so they should have known that burying on יום טוב was wrong.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 39 said they are not רשעים because they honestly thought burial was a מצוה. רב פפא argues that the נידוי should have ended that mistake. If they kept doing it after being warned this way, they cannot claim they did not know.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it so that... (opens a challenge)

phrases.english: But didn't we put them in נידוי?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא קָא מְשַׁמְּתִינַן לְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of Step 39 that the gravediggers honestly thought they were doing a מצוה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's claim that the gravediggers are not רשעים because they thought burial was a מצוה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The נידוי was a clear warning. Anyone who keeps doing the act after such a warning can no longer claim an honest mistake.

steps.title: They thought the נידוי was for atonement
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא answers that the gravediggers understood the נידוי as atonement the רבנן were doing for them, not as a punishment for a sin.
steps.simpleTranslation: They thought: the רבנן are making atonement for us.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא answers רב פפא. The gravediggers did not take the נידוי as a sign that they had sinned. They thought it was the רבנן's way of getting them a כפרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question was whether the נידוי took away their excuse of not knowing. The answer is no. In their minds they had done a good deed, and the נידוי was only like a cleansing step for touching a יום טוב issue. So they still were not knowingly doing wrong, and they stay valid witnesses.
steps.whatToRemember: Someone who breaks a law because he honestly thinks he is doing a מצוה is not a רשע, so he is not פסול לעדות. This stays true even if the רבנן punish him, as long as he misunderstands what the punishment means.

phrases.aramaic: סָבְרִי: כַּפָּרָה קָא עָבְדִי לַן רַבָּנַן.
phrases.english: They thought: the Sages are making atonement for us.

steps.triggerLanguage: סָבְרִי: כַּפָּרָה קָא עָבְדִי לַן רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב פפא's challenge in Step 40 and closes the gravediggers story.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the people's state of mind: the נידוי did not tell them they had sinned.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The נידוי should have shown them they were doing wrong, so they knowingly sinned.
steps.terutzMaskana: They saw the נידוי as a כפרה, not a rebuke, so they still thought they were doing a מצוה and stay valid witnesses.

steps.title: Opening a new statement
steps.stepSummary: The word איתמר introduces a new discussion of the אמוראים, which continues after this point.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated:
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא is starting a new topic and is about to quote what the אמוראים said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word איתמר tells us a new statement of the אמוראים is coming, often a מחלוקת. The content comes right after this word. It moves on from the gravediggers to a new question about witnesses, the עד זומם.

keyTerms.meaning: A witness proven false by other witnesses who say he was elsewhere (the upcoming topic)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't look for the content of the statement here. איתמר only opens it, and the actual words come next.

phrases.english: It was stated:

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיתְּמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the gravediggers story behind and opens a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No ruling yet. This line only introduces the next teaching of the אמוראים.
